why: A (universes 0, K : Type) is the project's corollary of Theorem 22.1 for slice submanifolds N ⊆ V (any model Z): if closed ρ-balls about p are compact, every unbroken geodesic p → q NOT OF LEAST ENERGY has formIndex (energyHessian) ≥ λ₀, and Ω^d (minPaths = paths of least energy) is a RETRACT OF AN OPEN NEIGHBOURHOOD in Ω, then π_K(Ω^d) → π_K(Ω) is bijective for |K|+2 ≤ λ₀ and onto for |K| < λ₀. B (abstract complete connected Riemannian ℝⁿ-manifolds, any Levi-Civita connection): if the separation quotient of Ω^d = E⁻¹[0, ρ(p,q)²] is a TOPOLOGICAL MANIFOLD and every NON-MINIMAL blind geodesic has variational index lam ≥ λ₀, the induced maps are bijective / onto (and multiplicative). A ⇒ B fails genuinely: abstract setting; even on embedded manifolds it needs Hanner's theorem (topological manifold ⇒ ANR ⇒ neighbourhood retract), which is formalized neither in the project nor in Mathlib, and the identification of B's variational index with formIndex (LamEq). B ⇒ A fails genuinely: A's retract hypothesis is weaker than B's manifold hypothesis (A covers non-manifold Ω^d), A allows any model Z, non-connected N and any finite K.
